title: Bài sưu tầm 138 - Passage 1: Mary Anning: Pioneer of Fossil Hunting on the Jurassic Coast
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 1 — TEST 138

Mary Anning: Pioneer of Fossil Hunting on the Jurassic Coast

Paragraph 1. Born in 1799 in the coastal town of Lyme Regis in southern England, Mary Anning grew up in an impoverished household where survival depended on ingenuity. Her father, Richard, was a cabinetmaker who supplemented his modest income by gathering fossilized shells along the crumbling limestone cliffs. Winter storms regularly triggered landslides along the coast, exposing ancient marine creatures buried for millions of years. Richard cleaned these 'curiosities' and sold them from a roadside table to passing tourists visiting the seaside resort.

Paragraph 2. When Mary was only eleven, her father died, leaving the family heavily in debt; from then on, fossil collecting became their sole means of support. Fortunately, Richard had taught Mary how to spot subtle outlines in dark shale and extract delicate bones with small hammers and chisels. In 1811, Mary’s older brother Joseph spotted a massive skull protruding from a cliff face, and over the following months Mary patiently chiselled out the complete five-metre skeleton beneath it.

Paragraph 3. At first, local scholars assumed the creature was a fossilized crocodile, since the scientific concept of extinction was still fiercely debated in Britain. Only later did anatomists recognize it as an Ichthyosaurus—a marine reptile unlike any living animal. A wealthy local landowner bought the skeleton for twenty-three pounds and arranged for it to be displayed in London. Anning continued scouring the slippery cliffs in all seasons, once narrowly escaping death when a falling rock killed her dog, Tray, beside her.

Paragraph 4. In 1823, Anning made an equally astonishing discovery: the first complete skeleton of a long-necked Plesiosaurus. When news reached Paris, the famous French anatomist Georges Cuvier initially suspected the find was a clever forgery until he examined a detailed drawing sent by Anning herself. Convinced by the accurate anatomy of the sketch, Cuvier publicly apologized and acknowledged the specimen as genuine. Five years later, Anning unearthed Britain’s first Pterodactylus—a flying reptile—and accurately identified fossilized coprolites as prehistoric animal droppings, revealing the ancient diet of marine predators.

Paragraph 5. Despite her unmatched field expertise, Anning remained an outsider in the formal world of science. As a working-class woman, she was barred from joining the Geological Society of London, which did not admit female members until 1904. Prominent male geologists frequently purchased her finest fossils and published groundbreaking academic papers on them without giving her written credits for her discoveries or anatomical insights. Yet her reputation among serious researchers was undeniable: when King Frederick Augustus II of Saxony visited Lyme Regis in 1844, he stopped specifically at her modest shop to purchase a specimen.

Paragraph 6. In her final years, after Anning fell ill with breast cancer, members of the Geological Society raised funds and persuaded the British government to grant her a modest annual pension. She died in 1847 at the age of forty-seven, largely overlooked by history books for over a century. In 2010, however, the Royal Society formally named her among the ten British women who have most profoundly shaped the history of science.

groups.title: Questions 8–13
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 8–13 on your answer sheet, write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "Winter storms regularly triggered landslides along the coast..."
Từ cần điền: storms.
Đoạn 1: "...sold them from a roadside table to passing tourists..."
Từ cần điền: tourists.
Đoạn 2: "...Mary’s older brother Joseph spotted a massive skull..."
Từ cần điền: brother.
Đoạn 3: "...local scholars assumed the creature was a fossilized crocodile..."
Từ cần điền: crocodile.
Đoạn 4: "...until he examined a detailed drawing sent by Anning herself."
Từ cần điền: drawing.
Đoạn 5: "...published groundbreaking academic papers on them without giving her written credits..."
Từ cần điền: credits.
Đoạn 6: "...persuaded the British government to grant her a modest annual pension."
Từ cần điền: pension.

q8.text: Following the death of her father, Mary's family relied entirely on selling fossils to survive.

steps: Đoạn 2: Khi cha mất để lại món nợ, săn hóa thạch trở thành nguồn sống duy nhất của gia đình (sole means of support).
Kết luận: Chọn TRUE.

q9.text: The landowner who bought the Ichthyosaurus later donated it permanently to a public museum in London.

steps: Đoạn 3: Bài chỉ nói địa chủ giàu mua bộ xương giá 23 bảng và đưa đi trưng bày ở London (arranged for it to be displayed in London), không nói ông có tặng vĩnh viễn cho bảo tàng công cộng hay không.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q10.text: Georges Cuvier travelled from Paris to England to verify the authenticity of the Plesiosaurus bones.

steps: Đoạn 4: Cuvier kiểm chứng qua bản vẽ chi tiết do chính Anning gửi sang chứ không đi từ Paris sang Anh kiểm tra xương thật (examined a detailed drawing sent by Anning herself).
Kết luận: Chọn FALSE.

q11.text: Women were not permitted to become official members of the Geological Society of London during Anning's lifetime.

steps: Đoạn 5: Hội Địa chất London không nhận thành viên nữ mãi đến năm 1904, trong khi Anning mất năm 1847.
Kết luận: Chọn TRUE.

q12.text: Despite her skill, Anning's fossil shop never attracted customers from outside Britain.

steps: Đoạn 5: Vua Frederick Augustus II của Saxony (ngoài nước Anh) đã ghé trực tiếp cửa hàng của bà năm 1844 để mua mẫu vật.
Kết luận: Chọn FALSE.

q13.text: The Royal Society has now funded a permanent memorial statue of Anning in Lyme Regis.

steps: Đoạn 6: Hội Hoàng gia vinh danh bà vào top 10 nữ khoa học gia tiêu biểu năm 2010, nhưng hoàn toàn không đề cập việc tài trợ tượng đài ở Lyme Regis.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.
